one_liner: C++ RPC framework on Sogou Workflow speaking SRPC, Thrift-framed and bRPC wire protocols; ~1.6-2.8x Apache Thrift server QPS.
what_it_does: SRPC is an IDL-driven RPC framework. You write a .proto or .thrift file, run protoc plus srpc_generator to get a *.srpc.h, derive from the generated Service, and register it on a server class that picks the wire protocol: SRPCServer, SRPCHttpServer (JSON over HTTP, callable with curl), ThriftServer (Thrift binary framed), ThriftHttpServer, BRPCServer or TRPCServer, each on its own port. Clients are generated per protocol and offer an async callback call, a blocking call with RPCSyncContext, and a WFFuture-returning async_ call. For Thrift IDL the generator keeps Apache-style handler signatures (void Echo(EchoResult& _return, const std::string& ...)) and a Thrift-style sync client with send_/recv_ methods, so porting is mechanical but not a drop-in.
how_it_is_fast: It runs on the Sogou C++ Workflow engine. Poller threads handle epoll/kqueue I/O and deserialize messages as bytes arrive, and a separate handler thread pool runs service methods and callbacks. Handlers never need to block a thread, because extra work goes into the request's SeriesWork as async tasks. Protobuf payloads are serialized through a ZeroCopyOutputStream straight into a chunked RPCBuffer (2 KB-256 KB pieces) that is handed to the socket as an iovec array for scatter-gather writes. Clients keep a keep-alive connection pool with one connection per in-flight request, and there is no pipelining. The README does not break down where the gap to Apache Thrift's TNonblockingServer comes from.
when_to_use: You run Apache Thrift C++ servers with TBinaryProtocol over framed transport at 16+ concurrent requests: SRPC's ThriftServer speaks the same wire format, and its charts show ~2x server QPS at 32-256 concurrent 1 KB requests on one machine.
One handler implementation must be served over several protocols at once, such as Thrift framed for legacy clients, bRPC-std, and HTTP+JSON for other languages.
RPC handlers call other backends (HTTP, other RPCs, timers) and you want to do this without blocking threads, by pushing Workflow tasks onto ctx->get_series().
Unary RPC with tail-latency targets at a fixed load: the README's CDFs show srpc under ~170 us to p99.9 on one machine at 10k QPS, while Apache Thrift sits at ~235-480 us.
You want the framework to handle gzip/zlib/snappy/lz4 compression and OpenTelemetry/Prometheus trace and metrics reporting.
when_not_to_use: You need gRPC wire compatibility or streaming RPC. SRPC speaks neither: gRPC support is an open TODO (issue #85), and maintainers call the lack of streaming a weak spot (#230).

Your Thrift setup uses TMultiplexedProtocol, several services on one port with native Thrift clients, oneway methods, or a protocol other than binary. ThriftServer implements only binary protocol over framed or HTTP transport, serves one Thrift service per port (#394), and the generator skips oneway methods (#100).

Low concurrency or blocking callers. At 1-8 in-flight requests the chart shows srpc only ~1.05-1.4x ahead of Apache Thrift, and a blocking caller thread gets at most about 1/RTT calls per second (maintainer, #376).

Many small requests on NICs with a packets-per-second limit, such as virtio VMs. SRPC has no single-connection pipelining mode. One user measured 56-75k cross-VM QPS against the README's ~500k, and brpc's single-connection mode did better in that setup (#376).
Your team does not want Workflow's callback/task programming model or a dependency on the Workflow engine. The library is also built with -fno-exceptions.

integration.form: static lib + shared lib (libsrpc.a / libsrpc.so) plus the srpc_generator code generator; CMake or Bazel; Debian (sid) and Fedora packages
integration.dependencies: Sogou Workflow (git submodule, v1.1.0 as of 2026-09), Protobuf >= 3.5 with protoc, OpenSSL (>= 1.1 recommended), zlib, snappy >= 1.1.6, lz4 (snappy and lz4 from submodules or system)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 on master since 2026-09-10 (protobuf 30+/abseil need it; earlier releases built as C++11/14); CMake >= 3.6; minimum compiler version not documented
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (needs Workflow's IOCP-based windows branch; srpc_tools unsupported there). Workflow claims x86 32/64-bit, big- and little-endian ARM, Loongson and Android.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for SRPC's public classes. Service methods run concurrently on Workflow's handler thread pool, and the benchmark issues calls on one shared client object from many callbacks. RPCBuffer is documented as not thread-safe. The Thrift-style sync status (thrift_last_sync_ctx) is per thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — ThriftServer/ThriftClient interoperate with Apache Thrift over binary protocol and framed transport, and the generated handlers keep Apache-style signatures. You still regenerate stubs with srpc_generator, change headers, base classes and the build, and lose multiplexed, non-binary and oneway support.

gotchas: The README charts are from before the 2020 open-source release (maintainer, #376). In a 2024 re-run on a 10-core box (same machine, 32 B requests, brpc protocol), maintainers measured srpc and pooled brpc at rough parity: about 124k-172k QPS for every client/server pairing.

SRPC has two Thrift modes. ThriftServer/ThriftClient (tutorials 07/08) speak native Thrift framed. SRPCServer with Thrift IDL (tutorials 03/04) uses SRPC's private protocol and cannot talk to Apache Thrift peers (#351, #394).

The Thrift IDL parser is hand-written and has broken on real IDLs. It dropped Hbase.thrift method parameters (fixed in PR #352), and issue #392 (bad code for two-level namespaces) is still open. Test your .thrift files before committing to a port.

v0.10.5 (2026-09-15) added a missing check of meta_len against payload length in BRPC/TRPC message parsing, so upgrade if you face untrusted peers. Master now requires C++17, but the README quick-start still compiles with -std=c++11.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SRPC over brpc when you need Apache Thrift framed-binary and bRPC-std interoperability from one set of handlers plus Workflow's async task model. SRPC's charts show it roughly level with brpc (slower on one machine, faster across machines), but brpc offers streaming and a single-connection mode. Pick grpcxx if you need gRPC wire compatibility; among the catalogued siblings only SRPC is measured against Apache Thrift.
verified_claims_summary: These are SRPC's own README charts from 2020, pre-open-source data. SRPC's async client drove empty-response echo servers, each with 16 IO and 16 handler threads, on a 2x8-core Xeon E5-2630 v3 with 128 GB and 10 GbE. srpc-std reached ~310k QPS vs ~145k for Apache Thrift TNonblockingServer (TBinaryProtocol) at 32 concurrent 1 KB requests on one machine (~2.1x), and ~470-520k vs ~167-220k across machines (~2.3-2.8x). The compiler and Thrift version are not stated; the build files show a CMake RelWithDebInfo build for SRPC and -O2 -g for the Thrift server.
status_note: Actively maintained: v0.10.5 came out on 2026-09-15 with commits the same month. It is Apache-2.0 with 2.1k stars and is packaged in Debian and Fedora. It is a normal built library, but it pulls in the whole Workflow engine.
